faqLeft.q: What engine does the Mercedes SL500/SL550 use?
faqLeft.a: It depends on the year. Early SL500s (R129) use the M113 5.0-litre V8. R230-generation cars use either the M113 or the M273 5.5-litre V8, depending on the year. R231 SL500/SL550 models use the M278 4.7-litre twin-turbo V8. Send us your registration and we'll confirm which one your car has.

faqLeft.q: How much does a Mercedes SL500/SL550 engine rebuild cost?
faqLeft.a: Rebuilds start from £4,500, for all three engine codes. Exact price depends on condition and parts required - submit your reg for a fixed-price quote.

faqLeft.q: Which engine code is fitted to my SL500/SL550?
faqLeft.a: Enter your registration on this page and we'll confirm whether you have the M113, M273 or M278 before you're quoted anything.

faqLeft.q: Do you rebuild M113 SL500 engines?
faqLeft.a: Yes. We replace valve seals, coolant components, timing chain and bearings as standard on every M113 rebuild.

faqLeft.q: Do you rebuild M273 SL500 engines?
faqLeft.a: Yes. The M273 shares the same V8 wear pattern as the M113, and we service it to the same standard.

faqRight.q: Do you rebuild M278 SL500/SL550 engines?
faqRight.a: Yes. The M278 twin-turbo V8 shows the same valve seal and coolant wear pattern over time, and we replace the same components as standard.

faqRight.q: Do you supply used SL500/SL550 engines?
faqRight.a: Yes, in some cases a matched low-mileage used engine is the right option. Our team will advise honestly once we've matched your registration and understood your situation.

faqRight.q: Can you recover my SL500/SL550 if the engine has failed?
faqRight.a: Yes - nationwide recovery is available from £70, and most vehicles are collected within a few hours of booking.

faqRight.q: How long does an SL500/SL550 engine rebuild take?
faqRight.a: Most rebuilds are completed within 3-5 working days from the time your car arrives at our workshop.

faqRight.q: Is rebuilding better than fitting a used engine?
faqRight.a: For most SL500/SL550 owners, yes. A rebuild removes the compatibility risk that comes with an unknown used unit's history, and comes with a 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty - often longer and more comprehensive than what a used engine supplier offers.
